prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a client restarts and reloads persisted tokens, the provider fails to silently refresh an expired access token and instead forces a full interactive re-authorization. #1784 fixes this at the root: `_initialize()` never called `update_token_expiry()` on the tokens loaded from storage, so `token_expiry_time` stayed `None` and the existing proactive-refresh check (which runs before any request is sent) always treated the stale token as valid, skipping refresh entirely. #2875 targets the same reported symptom but patches it reactively — it adds a new 'Step 3.5' inside the 401 handler in `async_auth_flow` that calls `_refresh_token()`/`_handle_refresh_response()` before falling through to full re-authorization. Notably, #2875's own inline comment states the reason it's needed: 'A provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time, so is_token_valid() treats the stale token as valid and the proactive-refresh branch above is skipped' — i.e. it explicitly names #1784's exact defect as the cause it is working around, rather than fixing it at the source. (2 PRs)

members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a client restarts and reloads persisted tokens, the provider fails to silently refresh an expired access token and instead forces a full interactive re-authorization. #1784 fixes this at the root: `_initialize()` never called `update_token_expiry()` on the tokens loaded from storage, so `token_expiry_time` stayed `None` and the existing proactive-refresh check (which runs before any request is sent) always treated the stale token as valid, skipping refresh entirely. #2875 targets the same reported symptom but patches it reactively — it adds a new 'Step 3.5' inside the 401 handler in `async_auth_flow` that calls `_refresh_token()`/`_handle_refresh_response()` before falling through to full re-authorization. (2 PRs)
